summary:
Masin Advisory Group, LLC (MAG) is a woman-owned, Houston-based boutique advisory firm founded and led by Natalie "Nat" Masin, CFA, CPA/ABV, CDFA. Its positioning is built around the "Triple Crown Advantage" — three integrated pillars: CFO Advisory, Transaction Advisory, and Managing Risk & Resolution (the site title reads "Masin Advisory Group | Triple Crown Advisory | Houston, TX"). The firm serves founder-owned businesses, private equity portfolio companies, and legal teams navigating financial disputes, and more broadly "business owners, executives, boards, and families facing complex financial decisions." It positions itself at inflection points: acquisitions, exits, restructurings, leadership transitions, functional transformation, and "matters requiring financial neutrality." The Risk & Resolution side blends forensic-adjacent financial analysis with ADR: named services include Divorce & Litigation Financial Analysis, Business & Employment Mediation, Valuation & Quality of Earnings, and risk work described as helping "identify risks and vulnerabilities, devise strategies to minimize risk, and formulate contingency plans." Natalie Masin is a mediator (Texas Association of Mediators candidate for full membership, 2026) with mediation practice areas spanning bankruptcy, business, family business, construction, insurance, probate/wills/trusts, real estate, and workplace/employment — so the practice covers disputes and forensic financial analysis with restructuring-adjacent work (bankruptcy mediation, capital structuring), rather than classic corporate restructuring.

The tone of voice is disciplined, calming, and credential-forward rather than aggressive litigation-support language: recurring phrases include "structure and disciplined analysis to situations where financial complexity, operational execution, and stakeholder considerations intersect," moving leadership teams "from ambiguity to alignment," "rigor and neutrality," and "empowering entrepreneurs and business leaders." Natalie's background — CFO of Groendyke Transport, leadership across publicly traded and PE-backed companies in energy, agriculture, and social services, UT Austin (Financial Reporting and Assurance) — reinforces an operator-turned-advisor persona: she has sat in the client's chair. An AI income-reconstruction engine pitches best as an instrument of that neutrality: defensible, transparent, mediation-ready analysis, not a black box.

Caveats: the proxy gateway blocked all direct access to masinadvisory.com (including /services/risk-resolution), so exact on-page copy for the Risk & Resolution page and visual brand details (colors, typography) could not be verified — brand cues below are inferred from the "Triple Crown" motif and boutique-professional positioning and should be confirmed against the live site or a brand kit before final delivery. Also note the naming hazard: masinproject.com is an entirely different global construction-disputes firm ("Masin"); do not borrow its language or credentials. Contact details on record: 32653 Giboney Road, Hempstead, TX 77445 (Hockley/Waller County, greater Houston), (832) 848-0413; member of the Greater Houston Women's Chamber of Commerce.

Firm identity: woman-owned, Houston-based, global reach; LLC address 32653 Giboney Road, Hempstead TX 77445; phone (832) 848-0413; GHWCC member listed under Management Consultants.

Forensic fit: 'Divorce & Litigation Financial Analysis' plus CDFA and CPA/ABV credentials make divorce income determination, lifestyle analysis, and business-owner true-income cases the natural first use case for an income-reconstruction engine.

Access caveat: masinadvisory.com and the /services/risk-resolution URL returned 403 through the proxy (gateway policy denial on CONNECT), so exact page copy and visual brand (colors/typography) are unverified; all quotes above come from search-index snippets of the site and third-party profiles.

terminology: Triple Crown Advantage — MAG's brand name for its three integrated pillars: CFO Advisory, Transaction Advisory, Managing Risk & Resolution.
Financial neutrality — MAG's framing for serving as an impartial financial analyst/mediator in disputes rather than a hired-gun advocate.
CDFA (Certified Divorce Financial Analyst) — credential for analyzing the financial issues of divorce: support income, asset division, tax effects.
CPA/ABV (Accredited in Business Valuation) — AICPA credential signaling qualification to value closely held businesses for litigation.
Income reconstruction — forensic determination of true economic income from indirect evidence when books/returns are unreliable.
Lifestyle analysis — reconciling a party's spending against reported income to expose unreported income (core CDFA/divorce technique).
Bank deposits method / net worth method / expenditures (source-and-application-of-funds) method — the classic IRS-recognized indirect methods of income reconstruction.
Quality of Earnings (QoE) — analysis of the sustainability and accuracy of reported earnings; a named MAG service line.
Normalization / add-backs — adjusting owner compensation and personal perquisites run through a business to state true economic earnings.
Perquisite (perk) analysis — quantifying personal benefits paid by a company to its owner, central in divorce and shareholder disputes.
Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) / mediation — resolving disputes outside court; MAG offers Business & Employment Mediation.
Community property characterization and tracing — Texas family-law analysis of which assets/income are marital vs. separate.
Exit readiness — preparing a founder-owned business for sale; MAG service 'M&A Execution & Exit Readiness'.
Schedule of findings / court-ready exhibit — the deliverable format a forensic accountant expects: numbered schedules with source-document tie-outs.
Daubert-defensible — methodology reliable enough to survive an expert-testimony admissibility challenge; the bar any AI-assisted analysis must clear.
demo_ideas: Name the demo as the third leg of their own brand: e.g., 'Crown Ledger' or 'MAG Resolve — Forensic Income Reconstruction Engine', subtitled 'Built for the third leg of the Triple Crown: Managing Risk & Resolution'.

Footer/watermark on every screen and exported schedule: 'Prepared for Masin Advisory Group, LLC — Risk & Resolution | Houston, TX' with a 'Confidential — Draft for Discussion' stamp, mirroring litigation-support work-product conventions.

Lead demo case matched to their client base: a founder-owned Houston services company in a divorce — owner reports $85K W-2 income but the engine reconstructs ~$400K true economic income via bank-deposits method, lifestyle analysis, and perk add-backs (auto, travel, family payroll) — exactly the Divorce & Litigation Financial Analysis + CDFA sweet spot.

Second case tab for the PE/legal-team audience: an earnout or partner-buyout dispute where the engine normalizes EBITDA and flags related-party leakage — ties Risk & Resolution to their Valuation & QoE and Transaction Advisory pillars.

Frame every output as 'mediation-ready': a one-page neutral summary exhibit both sides can read, echoing Natalie's mediator role and the firm's 'financial neutrality' and 'from ambiguity to alignment' language — position the AI as the neutral's instrument, not an advocate's weapon.

Show the defensibility layer explicitly: each reconstructed number click-through to its source documents (bank statements, GL lines, tax returns) with the named method (bank deposits / net worth / expenditures), so a CPA/ABV sees a Daubert-defensible audit trail rather than a black box.

Deliverable export named in their voice: 'Schedule of Findings — Reconstructed Income Analysis, Prepared under the direction of Natalie Masin, CFA, CPA/ABV, CDFA' (position AI as staff-level preparer, practitioner as reviewer/signer).

Visual co-branding: since site colors are unverified, use a restrained 'Triple Crown' prestige palette (deep navy or racing green with a gold accent, serif display type over a clean sans body) and include a one-click 'brand kit swap' to show you'll match their exact identity on engagement.
A subtle Triple Crown motif in the UI — three-step progress crown (Ingest > Reconstruct > Resolve) — so the product architecture itself mirrors their brand story.
Texas-specific touches that read as 'made for them': community-property characterization flags, Texas child/spousal support income definitions, and Harris County court exhibit formatting defaults.

Opening pitch slide framed in their own quoted language: 'Structure and disciplined analysis where financial complexity meets stakeholder considerations — now at machine speed', with an explicit line that the engine scales a solo-founder practice (MAG is effectively Natalie plus network) to big-four forensic throughput without headcount.
